title: Shopify's Architecture to Handle the World's Biggest Flash Sales (talk video with full transcript)
date: 2022-10-07 (InfoQ 'Recorded at'; tagged QCon Plus May 2022; same talk given at QCon London 2022-04-04)
description: Founder's seed. Card path: checkout iframe -> CardSink token -> monolith background job -> CardServer -> adapter library -> processor; checkout, orders and refunds stay in the monolith; idempotency keys plus Resumption step log; country-scoped circuit breakers; Packwerk polices payments-to-orders calls. Historical (pre-2023).

title: Shopify's architecture to handle the world's biggest flash sales (slide deck, QCon London 2022)
description: 57-slide PDF that goes with E001: slides 25-26 card flow (CardSink/CardServer/Processor), 44 benchmark gateway, 50 Semian key, 51 idempotent request fields, 52-54 Resumption recovery points. Session page https://archive.qconlondon.com/node/142606 (HTTP 200). Historical.

title: 10 Tips for Building Resilient Payment Systems
description: Centralized payment service reached from a checkout background job; correlation_id; idempotency keys (ULID, unique for 24h or less); reconciliation with anomaly records; merchant country added to circuit-breaker key; benchmark gateway for load tests. Historical.

title: Building Resilient GraphQL APIs Using Idempotency
description: Money Infrastructure's Payment Service (GraphQL; clients Shopify and Billing); ChargeCreate; idempotency key as required mutation input; IncomingRequest per client+key; recovery points split by side-effect type; 409 on concurrent duplicate. Historical.

title: Navigating Recurring Payments in India: A Backend Perspective
description: A market regulation (RBI e-mandates) absorbed inside the internal payment service used by Billing: source/charge model, provider token, provider receipt field used as idempotency key, UPI webhooks, internal gem shared across apps for one provider. About merchant billing, not buyer checkout. Historical.

title: High Availability by Offloading Work Into the Background
description: Background-job guarantees at Shopify: no exactly-once delivery, idempotent charge jobs make at-least-once safe, outbox and SAGA patterns, job parameters treated as a backward-compatible contract. General guidance, not a payments design doc. Historical.

title: Performance Testing At Scale—for BFCM and Beyond
description: States Shopify Core is a monolith supported by separate services including payment processing infrastructure; load tests check out through a mock payment gateway.

title: How we prepare Shopify for BFCM
description: 2025 readiness programme: payment processing listed among 'critical journeys' for game days; Toxiproxy fault injection; checkout queues backed up in early scale tests. Little on boundary design.

title: We replaced Redis with MySQL for inventory reservations—and it scaled
description: Checkout completion sequence: reserve inventory when payment starts, claim when payment succeeds, now in the same MySQL transaction as the inventory ledger; the old Redis split allowed payment/inventory mismatches; shadow mode and pod-by-pod rollout.

title: Powering Shopify's High-Performance, PCI DSS v4 Compliant Checkout with Sandboxing
description: Checkout front end: Shopify-managed parent page, app code in sandboxes behind a postMessage bridge, payment form in a separate 'payment page' iframe from a cardholder data environment. Shopify Partners blog, written by a Shopify Distinguished Engineer.

title: Google Pay inside sandboxed iframe for PCI DSS v4 compliance
description: Third-party (Google) post quoting Shopify: wallet code runs in a sandboxed iframe inside Shopify Checkout; Shopify passed its PCI DSS v4 audit this way.

title: Building the Universal Commerce Protocol
description: Open protocol co-developed with Google for agentic checkout: stable core checkout primitives, independently versioned capabilities and extensions, a checkout state machine with hand-off, payment handlers published by each provider and negotiated per transaction. An external contract, not a description of Shopify internals.

title: Introducing the commerce payments protocol
author_or_speaker: Conner Swenberg, Amie Corso (Coinbase); Simon Lacoursière (Shopify)
description: Onchain escrow protocol behind USDC in Shopify Payments: authorize, capture, charge, void, reclaim, refund with expiries and single-use signed payments. Shows a new rail fitted to authorize/capture semantics. Co-authored with Coinbase; republished from the Base blog.

title: Supporting Passkeys in Shop's Authentication Flows
description: Shop Pay is its own Rails system on the Shop domain and is embedded in merchant storefronts through an iframe.

title: Horizontally scaling the Rails backend of Shop app with Vitess
description: The buyer-side Shop app runs as a separate Rails backend sharded by user_id, unlike shop-sharded core; cross-shard transactions were split and made self-healing. Does not mention payments directly.

title: A Packwerk Retrospective
description: Candid review: privacy (public API) checks removed in Packwerk 3.0; domain components such as 'Checkouts' do not match how code runs; isolating one base package took months; Shopify discussed removing Packwerk. Cross-posted at https://shopify.engineering/a-packwerk-retrospective (2024-02-07, HTTP 200).

title: One engine, many tools — Introducing Rubydex
description: 2026 evidence that Packwerk still checks the core monolith and is being moved onto the Rubydex engine (about 3x more constant references resolved). Related: Rubydex linter post 2026-09-08 https://railsatscale.com/2026-09-08-introducing-rubydex-linter-structural-checks-for-ruby-projects/ (HTTP 200).

title: The Myth of the Modular Monolith (Rails World 2024, day 2 opening keynote)
description: Keynote reviewing six years of modularizing Shopify's monolith: coupling and deploys not improved, new problems such as primitive obsession. Video only (Rails World 2024 YouTube playlist, HTTP 200); no transcript found; slide text read on Speaker Deck (HTTP 200); spoken content not reviewed.

title: Under Deconstruction: The State of Shopify's Monolith
description: 37 components with public entrypoints; credit card vaulting kept as a separate service because of sensitive data; services split only for good reasons; pub/sub for dependency inversion; Sorbet for boundary contracts. Historical.

title: Enforcing Modularity in Rails Apps with Packwerk
description: Packwerk launch post: dependency and privacy checks; components are commerce domains such as orders and checkout; extracting microservices called a topology change; 48 packages in core. Historical.

title: Deconstructing the Monolith: Designing Software that Maximizes Developer Productivity
description: Origin of componentization (2017): components own their data and expose public APIs; Wedge tracked boundary violations; payments and orders were intertwined. Historical.

title: Shopify-Made Patterns in Our Rails Apps
description: Written by a Payments developer: one shared database for all domains, everything keyed to Shop, no database-level foreign keys, warnings when code crosses components; Monorail schema contracts for Kafka events. Historical.

title: Capturing Every Change From Shopify's Sharded Monolith
description: Log-based change data capture (Debezium, Kafka) from 100+ core shards; warns that CDC ties consumers to the source's internal data model. Data platform, not payments. Historical.

title: A Pods Architecture To Allow Shopify To Scale
description: Pods: groups of shops on isolated datastores; each request or job bound to one pod; Sorting Hat routing. Background for why payment work is shop-scoped. Historical.

title: Componentizing Shopify's Tax Engine
description: Analogous domain: tax carved into one component behind request/response schemas used by Cart, Checkout and Order, verified by a parallel 'experiment' code path before cutover. Not payments. Historical.

title: How We Enable Two-Day Delivery in the Shopify Fulfillment Network
description: Fulfilment analogue: the separate SFN app pushes precomputed delivery dates into core through GraphQL APIs so checkout does a local lookup; the promised date flows back at fulfilment. Not payments. Historical.

title: Creating a Flexible Order Routing System with Shopify Functions
description: Orders and fulfilment: market-specific routing rules written as Shopify Functions with GraphQL input and ranked output, run by core. A pattern for isolating variation; not payments.

title: Five Years of React Native at Shopify
description: One sentence on POS: the app syncs data in the background so it can process transactions while offline. Thin.

title: Building Reliable Mobile Applications (Shopify POS)
description: POS reliability: payment success is monitored by country, card network and card reader; payments has dedicated on-call. Thin. Historical.

title: Extensions for payments (Payments Platform overview)
description: Product docs. Third-party providers plug into checkout as approved payments extensions (five types) supporting charge, refund, authorize, capture and void; merchants switch off the legacy gateway. External contract, not internals.

title: Payments apps: implementation considerations
description: Product docs. Provider contract: mTLS, idempotency (keys never expire), resolve/reject mutually exclusive per id, app must retry 18 times over 24h, Shopify retries timed-out calls.

title: Payments app request reference
date: undated; accessed 2026-10-10 (fields added in API 2024-01 to 2024-10)
description: Product docs. What crosses to a provider: payment attempt id (the idempotency key), group per checkout, session_id, amount, currency, kind sale/authorization, no order ID; refunds point at the original payment_id.

title: OrderTransactionStatus and OrderTransactionKind enums (GraphQL Admin API)
description: Product docs. How a payment appears on an order: statuses include AWAITING_RESPONSE and UNKNOWN; kinds include AUTHORIZATION, CAPTURE, SALE, VOID, REFUND, EMV_AUTHORIZATION. Kind page https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/enums/OrderTransactionKind (HTTP 200).

title: Implementing idempotency (GraphQL Admin API)
description: Product docs. Public API idempotency: keys tracked for 24h, concurrent duplicates get IDEMPOTENCY_CONCURRENT_REQUEST, completed duplicates get the cached response.

title: Making idempotency mandatory for inventory adjustments and refund mutations
description: Changelog (breaking change): from API 2026-04, refundCreate and many inventory mutations fail at runtime without the @idempotent directive.

title: Payment Customization Function API
description: Product docs. Country and market rules about which payment methods appear are merchant/app Functions that return operations (hide, rename, reorder, terms, review), kept apart from payment processing.

title: Offline payments (Shopify POS)
description: Help docs. POS offline: the order is created with 'Payment pending', the card is processed after reconnecting, a later decline is flagged on the order; limits convert to local currency.

title: Shopify/packwerk (repository)
description: Boundary tool. README limits: only static constant references are checked, method calls ignored; public-API checker moved out to packwerk-extensions. github.com blocked here; README read via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/packwerk/main/README.md (200); versions https://rubygems.org/gems/packwerk/versions (200).

title: Shopify/semian (repository)
description: Circuit breaker and bulkhead library; 'dynamic' sub-resource names let one host map to several circuits, the mechanism the per-country payment keys in E001/E003 need (inference). README via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shopify/semian/main/README.md (200); versions https://rubygems.org/gems/semian/versions (200).

title: activemerchant/active_merchant (repository)
description: Gateway abstraction extracted from Shopify: one Ruby API over dozens of gateways. No source says it is the 'adapter library' in E001 (inference only). README via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/activemerchant/active_merchant/master/README.md (200); versions https://rubygems.org/gems/activemerchant/versions (200).
